operations.name: Passmore Williamson

expected.charges: Contempt of court for failing to produce Jane Johnson and her two sons after their escape from slavery in Philadelphia.
expected.convicted: Held in contempt by U.S. District Judge John K. Kane.
expected.sentence: Indefinite confinement until the contempt was purged; served one hundred days in Moyamensing Prison.

operations.source: Primary 1857 false-imprisonment proceedings, reproduced by Dickinson College: https://housedivided.dickinson.edu/ugrr/case_1855.html . July 27 commitment warrant resulted in arrest and imprisonment; this is the contempt arrest, not the earlier writ of habeas corpus.

operations.name: Justin D. Spry

expected.charges: Attempted arson of a police vehicle
expected.sentence: Sentenced to 24 months federal prison plus 3 years supervised release. On May 31, 2020 following Trenton, NJ protests, Spry, 21, was seen on video with Killian Melecio and Kadeem Dockery attempting to set fire to a police car; Spry was arrested at the scene while the others fled.

updates.prosecutor: Alexander E. Ramey; Michelle S. Gasparian
updates.plead: Guilty to attempting to obstruct, impede, or interfere with law enforcement officers during a civil disorder affecting commerce

operations.source: Primary October 21, 2021 sentencing report: https://www.justice.gov/usao-nj/pr/middlesex-county-man-sentenced-24-months-prison-interfering-law-enforcement-officers . Individual judge, prosecutors and plea explicitly documented. No prison admission inferred from sentencing.

operations.name: Channel Lewis

expected.charges: Federal conspiracy; lookout/driver in CVS pharmacy burglary during June 2020 Louisville unrest

updates.convicted: Yes; sentenced July 26, 2021 for conspiracy to commit burglary involving controlled substances

operations.source: Primary FBI Louisville report July 28, 2021: https://www.fbi.gov/contact-us/field-offices/louisville/news/press-releases/three-sentenced-for-pharmacy-burglary . Individual seven-month sentence confirms conviction; no actual custody endpoint inferred.

operations.name: Steven M. Fitch

expected.charges: Unlawful possession of a destructive device (Molotov cocktail classified as a firearm under the National Firearms Act, 26 U.S.C. § 5845(f)) — found on his person during BLM protests in downtown Omaha, Nebraska, May 31, 2020
expected.judge: U.S. District Judge Brian C. Buescher, District of Nebraska
expected.sentence: 30 months federal prison; 3 years supervised release

updates.plead: Guilty on October 27, 2020 to unlawful possession of a destructive device

operations.source: Primary actual sentencing and plea reports: https://www.justice.gov/usao-ne/pr/protester-sentenced-being-possession-molotov-cocktail and https://www.justice.gov/usao-ne/pr/iowa-man-pleads-guilty-being-possession-molotov-cocktail-during-omaha-protests . Sentence day is not treated as prison admission.

operations.name: H. R. Hanson

expected.charges: Federal prosecution under the Espionage Act of 1917 and/or the Sedition Act of 1918.
expected.convicted: Yes — the record states a sentence received and a term served at San Quentin State Prison.

operations.source: Stephen M. Kohn, American Political Prisoners (1994), page 162, individual H. R. Hanson entry: https://dokumen.pub/american-political-prisoners-prosecutions-under-the-espionage-and-sedition-acts-0275944158-9780275944155.html . Imposed term is not actual time served. Existing generic federal charge conflicts with state San Quentin context; preserved and flagged.

operations.name: Shamai Kedem Leibowitz

expected.charges: One count of knowingly and willfully disclosing classified communications intelligence, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 798(a)(3).
expected.sentence: 20 months imposed May 24, 2010 followed by three years supervised release. Physical-prison release remains recorded only at 2011 year precision: a June 5, 2012 report reproduces his firsthand statement that he left minimum-security prison nearly a year earlier. BOP register 50835-037 gives a later January 13, 2012 federal-custody endpoint; that does not replace the earlier physical-prison exit. Exact admission, prison-exit day and halfway-house transitions remain unresolved. The 609-day sentence conversion is not documented actual imprisonment.

updates.prosecutor: Steven M. Dunne; Kathleen M. Kedian

operations.source: Primary DOJ May 24, 2010 report reproduced by FAS: https://sgp.fas.org/news/2010/05/fbi052410.html . Both attorneys explicitly prosecuted this case. Future surrender order is not evidence of actual admission; existing qualified release information preserved.
